text: Good morning and welcome to Johnson & Johnson's third quarter 2026 earnings conference call.

conference. This call is being recorded. If anyone has any objections, you may disconnect at this
time. If you experience any technical difficulties during the conference, you may press star zero to
reach the operator. I will now turn the conference call over to Johnson & Johnson. You may begin.
Hello, everyone. This is Ryan Kors, Vice President of Investor Relations for Johnson & Johnson.
Welcome to our company's review of business results for the third quarter of 2026 and our financial outlook for the full year.
First, a few logistics.
As a reminder, today's presentation and associated schedules are available on the Investor Relations section of the Johnson & Johnson website at investor.jnj.com.

other things, the company's future operating and financial performance, market position,
and business strategy.
Your caution not to rely on these forward-looking statements, which are based on the current
expectations of future events using the information available as of the date of this recording.

to differ materially from those projected.
The description of these risks, uncertainties, and other factors can be found in our SEC filings,
including our 2025 Form 10-K, which is available at investor.jnj.com and on the SEC's website.
Additionally, several of the products and compounds discussed today are being developed
in collaboration with strategic partners or licensed from other companies.
This slide acknowledges those relationships.
Moving to today's agenda, Joaquin DeWato, our Chairman and CEO,
will discuss our business performance and growth drivers.
I will then review the third quarter sales and P&L results.
Joe Walk, our CFO, will then close by sharing an overview of our capital allocation priorities
and updated guidance for 2026.
Tom Kavanaugh, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, Innovative Medicine,
John Reed, Executive Vice President, Innovative Medicine Research and Development,
and Tim Schmid, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Chairman, MedTech, will be joining us for Q&A.
To ensure we provide enough time to address your questions, we anticipate the webcast will last approximately 60 minutes.
With that, I will now turn the call over to Joaquin.
Thank you, Ryan, and good morning, everyone.
Our strong performance in the third quarter reinforces our confidence in 2026 as a year of accelerated growth and impact for Johnson & Johnson.
In Q3, we reported operational sales growth of 6%, ahead of analyst consensus, and increased
sequential growth compared to the second quarter.
With six strategic focus areas, oncology, immunology, neuroscience, cardiovascular surgery
and vision, we are leading in areas of higher med need where innovation can make the greatest
difference for patients.
Our powerful combination of innovative medicine and medtech expertise strengthens our competitiveness.
Twenty-nine of our products and platforms now generate at least $1 billion in annual sales.
Our marketed portfolio continues to perform, our launches are gaining significant traction,
and we are advancing our new product pipeline that will sustain our growth into the next decade.
With sales in the quarter of more than $25 billion,
we are on track to meet our guidance and exceed $100 billion in annual revenue
for the first time in our company's 140-year history.
As we advance our differentiated portfolio and pipeline,
we have a clear path to double-digit growth by the end of the decade.
In innovative medicine, we delivered operational sales growth of 7.9% with eight brands growing double digits.
Let's start with oncology.
We are making progress to redefine cancer care from treatment to cure.
In the third quarter, our oncology business grew approximately 17%.
Our multiple myeloma portfolio and pipeline are unmatched,
with 80% of patients receiving a Johnson & Johnson therapy as part of their treatment journey.
And we continue to strengthen the body of evidence supporting our recently launched
multiple myeloma therapies and combination regimens.
New Phase III results announced in July demonstrated that the combination
of tegvili plus talve reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 89% as early as the second
line of treatment. In solid tumors, sales of riboban increased by 64%, reflecting its strength
in lung cancer. And by the end of the year, we expect to receive U.S. FDA approval for riboban
FASPRO in advanced head and neck cancer, a disease with significant unmet needs.
In bladder cancer, Inlexo has rapidly emerged as a market leader for new patient share,
just one year after its launch.
Nearly one in three eligible patients started on an Inlexo regimen in the third quarter,
demonstrating its growing role in transforming care in high-risk, non-muscle-invasive disease.
During the quarter, we also invested to bolster our oncology pipeline.
We completed our acquisition of Firefly Bio, adding a promising new degraded antibody conjugate platform
that targets drivers of difficult-to-treat cancers, including KRAS.
Our ambition is to become the number one oncology company by 2030, with sales projected to exceed $50 billion.
Turning to immunology, we are building on our 25-year legacy to drive industry-leading innovation for patients.
Trenfaya delivered exceptional sales growth of 68% in the quarter, reflecting strong momentum
across its indications.
In the U.S., it is now the number one IL-23 inhibitor in new to brand share in Crohn's
disease, ulcerative colitis, and psoriatic arthritis.
And we continue to generate evidence that reinforces Trenfaya's clinical differentiation,

Based on the landmark STARS study, TREMFAYA is the first and only IL-23 inhibitor to demonstrate positive outcomes in axial disease clinical trials, including significant improvement in spinal pain, stiffness, and inflammation in patients with psoriatic arthritis.
This momentum reinforces our conviction in Trenfaya as a foundational medicine in inflammatory bowel and psoriatic diseases, and our belief that it can grow into a $10 billion plus franchise.
Icotide, our first-in-class targeted oral peptide for plaque psoriasis, continues to outpace recent competitors' launches.
More than 20,000 patients have initiated therapy through nearly 9,000 prescribers since Icotide's launch in the U.S.
We continue to make strong progress on commercial access with Icotide now broadly covered across all national plans.
Also this quarter, IMMAVI was approved as the first advanced treatment specifically for warm, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, a rare, life-threatening disease that causes severe anemia and fatigue.
This new indication builds on IMMAVI's momentum in generalized myasthenia gravis and reflects its broad potential across autoantibody diseases.
And we continue to pursue next-generation therapies.
In July, we announced a collaboration with SAIL Biomedicines to advance in vivo CAR-T approaches for immune-mediated diseases.
Next, in neuroscience, we aim to transform the future of brain health by addressing complex nervous system disorders.
Today, we are the definitive leader in neuropsychiatry.
Kaplaita reached $1 billion in year-to-date sales, making it our $29 billion platform.
Driven by strong uptake as an adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder, Kaplaita is now the fastest-growing oral branded therapy in this space.
And last month, we presented pivotal Phase III data that show Kaplaita significantly and rapidly improved symptoms of bipolar mania.
Spravato also delivered impressive growth of 36% this quarter, reflecting strong demand in treatment-resistant depression.
Now, let's turn to MedTech, where we deliver Q3 operational sales growth of 2.5%.
While we fell short of our expectations for the segment, our conviction in our future direction has not changed.
Starting with cardiovascular, we continue to invest in heart recovery, circulatory restoration,
and heart rhythm disorders to address the leading global cause of death.
This was another strong quarter for Shockwave, our circulatory restoration business, which grew 17%.
The ongoing global launch of Shockwave C2 Arrow continues to broaden the reach
of our intravascular lithotripsy platforms.
BodyPulse, our pulsed field ablation platform, reached a major milestone this quarter with more than 100,000 AFI patients treated worldwide.
BodyPulse Pro, which delivers five times faster ablation speed, has been very well received in Europe, where it is driving double-digit growth.
And just last week, we received approval for BodyPulse Pro in Japan.
With increasing clinical experience, we are seeing differentiated benefits from body pulse.
In a recent retrospective analysis, body pulse demonstrated a 68% lower risk of adverse cardiac events compared to a competing pulsed field ablation platform.
And in heart recovery, while physician selectivity continued to affect the biomed performance,
we remained confident in the technology and focused on supporting appropriate patient selection.
In surgery, we were poised to shape the next era of care through robotics,
digital innovation, and advanced instrumentation.
In July, the U.S. FDA granted de novo authorization for Taba,
the world's first stable integrated soft-tissue robotic system.
This is one of the most significant METEC innovations we will bring to market this decade.
Otava's unique architecture, automated features, and next-generation robotic instruments
help address surgeon needs for operating room space and better surgical workflows.
Its connection to our open digital ecosystem, Polyphonic, turns procedure data into actionable insights for clinicians.
We already signed our first commercial customer for Otava, and we are progressing our development program.
Our investigational device exemption trial is already underway in inguinal hernia repair.
with future plans for indication expansion into urology and gynecology.
Finally, in vision, we are advancing lifelong eye health
to bring better sight to more than 40 million people each year.
The recent U.S. launch of Technis Pure-C
further strengthened our portfolio of intraocular lenses.
During the quarter, Technis Pure C and Technis Odyssey surpassed 1 million implants worldwide, reflecting continued surgeon adoption and our leadership in personalized vision solutions.
We also received CE marking for Acuvue Oasis Max 2-Week reusable lenses, expanding our Acuvue portfolio in Europe.
Overall, this quarter's strong results demonstrate the impact of the choices we have made
to build a foundation for durable growth.
We sharpened our portfolio to focus on innovation with the greatest potential to change lives.
We proved our ability to grow through a significant loss of exclusivity.
Our strategic investments in high-growth areas are delivering results,
and our innovation engine continues to drive breakthroughs for patients.
That is why we have the confidence to say that we will finish 2026 strong
and that 2027 will be an even better year for Johnson & Johnson.
I will now turn the call back over to Ryan.
Thank you, Joaquin.
Moving to our financial results.
Unless otherwise stated, the percentages quoted represent operational results.
and therefore exclude the impact of currency translation.
Starting with Q3 2026 sales results.
Worldwide sales were $25.4 billion for the quarter, increasing 6%.
Growth in the U.S. was 9.1% and 1.8% outside the U.S.
Acquisitions and divestitures had a net negative impact on worldwide growth of 10 basis points.
Now turning to earnings.
For the quarter, net earnings were $210 million, and diluted earnings per share were $0.09 versus $2.12 a year ago.
Results in the quarter were impacted by the proposed talc litigation resolution,
as well as expenses associated with the Firefly biotransaction and Sale Biomedicine's collaboration, amounting to approximately $7 billion.
Adjusted net earnings for the quarter were $6.3 billion, and adjusted diluted earnings per share were $2.59.
cents, representing a decrease of 6.8% and 7.5% respectively, compared to the third quarter of
2025. Adjusted earnings in the quarter were also impacted by expenses associated with the Firefly
biotransaction and sale biomedicines collaboration. I will now comment on business sales results in
the quarter, focusing on the six key areas where meaningful innovation and strong commercial
execution are driving our performance and fueling long-term growth. Beginning with innovative
medicine, where our financial results reflect the depth of our expertise and innovation in
areas of high unmet need across oncology, immunology, and neuroscience. Worldwide sales
of $16.8 billion increased 7.9%, which underscores the continued strength of our key brands and new
launches. Growth in the U.S. was 11.1% and 3% outside the U.S. Divestitures had a negative
impact of 10 basis points on worldwide growth. In oncology, starting with multiple myeloma,
Darzalex growth was 15.6%, primarily driven by strong share gains of 5 points across all lines
of therapy, with 10 points in the frontline setting, as well as continued market growth,
partially offset by OUS pricing headwinds. Pervicti achieved growth of 35.2%, driven by
share gains across earlier lines of therapy and continued site expansion.
TechValley growth was 77.3%, driven by launch uptake and share gains across earlier lines
of therapy following last quarter's approval in the U.S. for TechValley Plus Darzalex
FastPro with U.S. growth greater than 100%.
Talve growth was 42.1%, driven by share gains due to increased depth of prescribing in the
community setting.
In lung cancer, RibroVant plus LastGlues delivered growth of 63.5%,
with strong share gains in the first and second lines driven by continued launch uptake in all regions,
along with rapid uptake in RibroVant FastPro.
In prostate cancer, Erleada delivered growth of 9.4%,
with continued share gains and market growth partially offset by unfavorable patient mix.
Within immunology, Trimphia delivered impressive growth of 68.2%,
driven by continued momentum from the IBD launch, with four points of share growth in both ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, alongside continued market growth.
Stelara declined 54%, which reflects continued competitive pressures from biosimilars and the ongoing shift towards novel classes.
Growth in other immunology is driven by a MAVE and Icotide launch uptake in the U.S.
In neuroscience, Spravato grew 36%, driven by continued share gains reflecting strong
physician adoption and increased patient demand.
Kaplita showed significant growth of 66.1%, driven by strong continued launch momentum
in adjunctive major depressive disorder and continued demand increases across bipolar
disorder and schizophrenia.
Now moving to MedTech.
Worldwide sales of $8.6 billion increased 2.5%, with growth of 4.8% in the U.S. and 0.1% outside the U.S.
Overall cardiovascular grew 4.1%, including 20 basis points related to acquisitions.
Electrophysiology delivered growth of 4.4%, driven by procedure expansion, commercial execution, and new product performance,
partially offset by competitive PFA pressures, which were more pronounced in ASPAC this quarter,
as well as a lapping of prior year OUS inventory dynamics.
Abium had saw a decline of 1.5% due to lower patient volume.
There are encouraging signals in the U.S. performance with improvement in the quarter,
supported by acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, and Impella 5.5 continuing to gain adoption.
Shockwave grew double digits at 17.2%.
driven by continued adoption of coronary and peripheral products as well as new product launches
and the reimbursement in the office-based lab setting within the U.S.
Surgery saw a decline of 1%, including a negative impact of approximately 30 basis points from divestitures.
The decline is more notably driven by ongoing expansion of EVP in China,
surgery transformation program outcomes across the portfolio,
and Middle East disruption which impacted tender timing and ordering patterns.
The decline was partially offset by portfolio strength, driven by recent innovations such as Ethicon 4000 and Dualto, as well as commercial execution and biosurgery.
Envision growth was 5.1%, driven by premium innovation, strong execution, and global reach.
Contact lenses and other products grew 4.3%,
driven by strong performance in the AccuView Oasis one-day family of products,
further solidifying our leadership position, partially offset by U.S. inventory dynamics.
Surgical vision delivered growth of 7.1%, driven by new product innovations,
robust demand for premium IOLs, and strong commercial execution,
partially offset by market-specific factors such as disruptions in the Middle East.
Orthopedics growth for the quarter was 3.4%, primarily driven by new product launches such
as Volt and Trauma and Emphasis and HIPS, including strong commercial execution and
vellus pull-through in knees.
Now turning to our consolidated statement of earnings for the third quarter of 2026.
I'd like to highlight a few noteworthy items that have changed compared to the same quarter
of last year.
Cost of goods sold deleveraged by 150 basis points driven by unfavorable product sales
mix and increased intangible asset amortization expense in the innovative medicine segment for
intracellular, partially offset by the impact of tariff recoveries in the medtech business.
Selling, marketing, and administrative expenses were flat as a percent of sales,
reflecting consistent commercial investments in the innovative medicine business.
We continue to invest strategically in research and development, deploying approximately 4.7
billion or 18.3% of sales, which includes $1 billion related to the acquisition of Firefly
Bio. In-process research and development impairment costs of $339 million in the quarter
is related to the write-off of Precardia, a non-core asset acquired as part of the broader
Abiumid transaction. Other income and expense was a net expense of $5.8 billion as compared to $478
million of income in the third quarter of 2025, with the change primarily driven by the proposed
Talc Litigation Resolution, and orthopedic separation-related costs.
The tax rate was a small net benefit in the quarter, primarily related to the positive
tax effect associated with the accrual for the proposed Talc Litigation Resolution.
More information can be found in our upcoming 10Q for changes in taxes.
Lastly, I'll direct your attention to the box section of the slide where we have also
provided our income before tax, net earnings, and earnings per share adjusted to exclude
the impact of intangible amortization expense and special items.
Now let's look at the adjusted income before tax by segment for the quarter.
Innovative medicine margin declined from 44.3% to 35.4%, primarily due to acquired in-process
research and development expense of approximately $1 billion related to the acquisition of Firefly
Bio, transaction costs for sale biomedicine, and unfavorable product sales mix and cost
of products sold.
MedTech margin increased from 21% to 22.9% driven by the impact of tariff recoveries
partially offset by increased strategic investments in commercial capabilities.
As a result, adjusted income before tax for the enterprise as a percentage of sales
decreased from 35.2% to 30.2%.
This concludes the sales and earnings portion of the call, and I will now turn the call over to Joe.
Thanks, Ryan.
Hello, everyone, and thank you for joining us today.
As you heard from Joaquin and Ryan, our third quarter results were driven by the strength of our innovative medicine business.
This performance more than offset headwinds in certain areas of medtech,
enabling us to exceed expectations on both the top and bottom line,
while continuing to invest in our pipeline and future growth.
We are clear on where medtech performance needs to improve,
specifically cardiovascular and surgery outside the U.S.,
and are taking action to strengthen results.
While disappointing, the underlying fundamentals of the MedTech business remain strong,
supporting our confidence in the long term for that business.
Across Johnson & Johnson, the drivers underpinning our outlook remain firmly in place.
As a result, we are raising our guidance for 2026 versus our most recent update in July.
The depth of our portfolio, momentum from new product launches,
and upcoming pipeline catalysts further reinforce our conviction in achieving double-digit growth
by the end of this decade with sustainable growth beyond.
Turning to financial metrics and our cash position, we ended the third quarter with
approximately $17 billion of cash and marketable securities and approximately $45 billion of debt
for a net debt position of approximately $28 billion, generating more than $6 billion in
free cash flow in the third quarter. We remain confident in our full-year free cash flow guidance
of approximately $21 billion. During the quarter, we completed the $1 billion acquisition of Firefly
Bio, deepening capabilities in oncology with next-generation antibody engineering to address
complex tumor biology. As Joaquin referenced earlier, we also entered into a collaboration
with sale biomedicines to advance in vivo CAR-T therapies for immune-mediated diseases.
Our disciplined approach to capital allocation is principled on prioritizing investments that
support key commercial launches, accelerating future innovation, increasing our annual dividend,
and strengthening our pipeline through strategic value-creating inorganic opportunities.
In July, we announced an agreement for a resolution of the ovarian talc litigation
for $5.5 billion, which is reflected in our third quarter gap results. The agreement is
conditioned upon the express participation of at least 95% of the remaining ovarian claims.
We are trending to meet the 95% threshold. Let me now turn to full year 2026 guidance.
As always, our outlook reflects what we know today regarding foreign exchange rates,
the broader macroeconomic environment and other external factors. Based on our year-to-date
performance and expectations for the fourth quarter, we are raising the midpoint and tightening
the range of our operational sales guidance. We now expect full-year operational sales growth
in the range of 6.7% to 7.1%, which represents operational sales of $100.7 billion at the midpoint
or growth of 6.9%. We do not speculate on future currency movements. As of last week,
the euro spot rate to the U.S. dollar was 1.12. However, the average rate for the fiscal year
stands at 1.15. Based on that average rate, we estimate reported sales growth of 7.2%
to 7.6%, with a midpoint of $101.2 billion, or 7.4%. Assuming the current spot rate holds into
next year, you could expect currency to be a headwind. Turning now to other items of the P&L.
Regarding operating margin, we now expect a decline of approximately 60 basis points.
This is an improvement from the 75 basis points decline reflected in our updated July guidance
that included the impact of the Firefly Bio and SAIL Biomedicine's transactions,
which had an unfavorable impact of 150 basis points.
Absent those deals, we continued to deliver base margin improvement.
As a reminder, our pre-tax adjusted operating margin outlook
also reflects the costs associated with the 53rd week of operations
and our previously announced agreement with the U.S. government
to improve access to medicines.
For net interest expense, we are lowering our guidance to $150 million to $200 million.
We are also tightening the range of our effective tax rate guidance.
Based on our year-to-date results, we now expect a full-year effective tax rate of 17.0% to 17.5%.
Given those updates, we now expect adjusted operational earnings per share
in the range of $10.95 to $11.05, or 2% at the midpoint.
We expect reported adjusted earnings per share of $11.05 to $11.15,
with a midpoint of $11.10, or growth of 2.9%.
Excluding the impact of FireflyBio and SaleBioMedicine's transactions of $0.64,
reported EPS growth would approach 9%.
As a reminder for your 2027 modeling, we expect Firefly Bio and Sale Biomedicines to have a combined dilutive impact of $1.36 per share on a full year adjusted earnings per share next year.
We will provide more details on our 2027 outlook later this year at our enterprise business review.
Let me now highlight several upcoming developments that reinforce our growth outlook and performance for the remainder of the year.
In oncology, we expect several important data readouts in the fourth quarter.
These include data for passeridomig, a first-in-class bispecific antibody in patients with advanced prostate cancer who have progressed after multiple lines of therapy.
We also expect data for JNJ6143, an investigational first-in-class once-daily oral therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
We continue to see strong adoption for anlexo with year-to-date sales of approximately $200 million
and expect to build on that momentum with a data readout in high-risk, non-muscle invasive bladder cancer later this year.
We also expect U.S. approval of Riborant FastPro in advanced head and neck cancer.
In immunology, as Joaquin referenced earlier, Icotide is off to a strong start
and we look forward to presenting data in psoriatic arthritis later this year.
In MedTech, we expect U.S. approval of Varipulse Pro in the fourth quarter, further complementing
last week's approval in Japan.
In heart recovery, we are taking corrective action to improve Abiomed's performance.
We continue to invest in clinical evidence and expect results from the HRPCI PROTECT4
trial in 2027.
The trial will have 1,252 patients, four times more than the CHIP-BESOS-3 study.
This large-scale study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of Abiomed's Impella CP pump during high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention.
In surgery, we are focused on commercializing Otava following its recent FDA de novo authorization.
We expect adoption and revenue contribution to build over time, with the goal of establishing Otava as a significant pillar of our surgery portfolio by the end of the decade.
Regarding orthopedics, we remain on track for the planned separation of the Pew Synthes by mid-2027.
I'm really proud of the team working to evaluate all separation vehicles,
and all options are better positioned today than when we announced our intentions with this business.
Given the way the Pew Synthes is performing and the momentum the Malnawana and his team are generating,
we are leaning towards a spin as being the best option to create long-term value for Johnson & Johnson shareholders.
That has always been our base plan, and we are confident that it can be successfully executed.
We will provide additional updates as appropriate and when there is more information to share.
Finally, I am really looking forward to and hope you join us for the Enterprise Business Review on December 8th.
At that event, we will provide additional perspective on our 2027 outlook and the key drivers that reinforce our conviction in achieving double-digit growth by the end of the decade.
Perhaps more importantly, we will highlight our earlier stage pipeline
and how it represents the next wave of growth into the next decade.
Attendees will also have the opportunity to experience firsthand
some of our latest innovations, such as OTAVA.
2026 is on track for another successful year,
exceeding expectations set at the beginning of the year.
We look forward to closing out 2026 strong and setting up 2027 for continued success.
Thank you to our colleagues whose dedication and commitment continue to advance innovation,
improve patient outcomes, and create long-term value for shareholders.
With that, we are ready to answer your questions.

Jennifer leaves Innovative Medicine incredibly well positioned,
